Saint Martin’s Island travel guide 2026–27: Dates, fees, and tourist restrictions
item.description:
After a long wait, Saint Martin’s Island is set to reopen to tourists. Visitors will be allowed to travel to the coral island from 1 November to 15 March next year. However, overnight stays will be permitted only in December and January. Tourists will also need a travel pass to visit the island.

The information was announced in a directive issued by the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change on 25 October. Under the directive, tourist vessels will continue to depart for Saint Martin’s Island from the Inland Water Transport Authority (BIWTA) jetty at Nuniyachhara in Cox’s Bazar town, as before.

However, the daily cap on tourist arrivals has been increased this year. A maximum of 3,500 tourists will be allowed to visit Saint Martin’s Island each day. Each visitor will have to pay an environmental conservation fee of Tk 100.

An interministerial meeting on tourist access to Saint Martin’s Island was held at the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change on 12 October. On 25 October, the ministry’s Environment-2 wing issued directives to the relevant ministries and departments to implement the decisions taken at the meeting. The directives retain the provisions of a notification issued by the ministry on 22 October 2025.

Under the 2025 notification, tourists will be allowed to visit Saint Martin’s Island only during the daytime in November and must return on the same day. Overnight stays will be permitted in December and January.

Sabreena Rahman, senior assistant secretary at the ministry, told Prothom Alo, “The provisions of the previous notification will be followed.”

This means that although the period during which tourists can visit Saint Martin’s Island has been extended this year, the rules governing overnight stays will remain unchanged from last year.

Meanwhile, tourists will again need a travel pass to visit Saint Martin’s Island. An official of the Bangladesh Tourism Board told Prothom Alo that visitors would need to obtain a travel pass, as they did last year. Technical preparations are underway in this regard.

Last year’s notification also imposed several restrictions to protect the island’s environment and biodiversity. These include:

  • No lights may be switched on at night on the beach or in adjoining areas.

  • Activities that generate noise and the organisation of barbecue parties are prohibited.

  • Entry into the keya forests, as well as the collection, purchase and sale of keya fruit, is prohibited.

  • Activities that harm the island’s biodiversity—including sea turtles, birds, corals, snails, mussels, starfish, horseshoe crabs, seagrass and algae—are prohibited.

  • Motorcycles, jet skis and similar vehicles are prohibited on the beach.

Syed Abul Maksud: Raconteur of Bangalee’s behaviour at micro level
item.description:
A few days ago several of my colleagues and I were returning home by a CNG-run auto-rickshaw after our scheduled office time at night. It was around 11:30 pm. Any regular commuter on Dhaka roads knows this is not a peak hour for traffic, but not lean time either. This is such a time when drivers of public transports in Dhaka try to showcase their skill in speed after driving the vehicle rather slowly the whole day.

At such a time, our auto-rickshaw driver was also not immune to the temptation. He showed his talent as sped past the Aarong Intersection at the western end of wide Manik Mia Avenue disobeying the traffic light. Awed, I just asked, “Bhai, what have you done! There was a red light there. You should have waited for the light to turn green.” The driver, however, in a rather casual tone answered, “Bhai, there is no traffic rule after 11:00 pm.”

Listening to his response to my worries, I thought about reporting this to the supervisor of our office’s transport department. Maybe this could be a solution for one driver but what could be the remedy of this startling collective idea of transport drivers that “There is no traffic rule after 11:00 pm.”

Upon reaching home, I disembarked the CNG-run auto-rickshaw and said to the driver, “Listen, you said ‘there is no traffic rule after 11:00 pm.’ What if another driver of a larger vehicle were there at that time and thought the same and violated the traffic lights. Could you imagine the result?” He did not feel the necessity to respond verbally to what I said. He just shrugged, closed the door of the backseat and went away.

Standing there at the entrance of the building where I live, after a very long time I recalled some words I read in a newspaper article written by Syed Abul Maksud in Prothom Alo, most probably in 2007. He wrote, as far as I can remember, “It is very easy to call politicians names as they are easily identifiable because they are not even 1 per cent of the population. But the mass of people of more than 99 per cent remain hidden in a mist; we cannot identify them or hold them accountable for anything. It is this hidden mass that mostly defines the zeitgeist, not the otherwise.”

Syed Abul Maksud wrote many books and articles based on his research and profuse study. Those range from philosophical musings to education, literature, social issues and feminism. He was also a regular columnist to several newspapers and those articles were not just fillers.

Maybe, just maybe, you can correct the behaviour of one driver or a few drivers through punitive actions but what about the mass of not only transport drivers but normal youths and many others, who take pride in violating the traffic rules.

The article presented a comparative discussion of actions by Bangalees during and after the Liberation War and the people of Vietnam after their war with the US. That article, more specifically the last few sentences of the article expanded my horizon to a great degree that would have otherwise taken a huge amount of reading and meditating on those for a rather long time. Once again, I realised the value of the life and writings of Syed Abul Maksud, who was rather laconic, as has been described by his friends and acquaintances.

Syed Abul Maksud wrote many books and articles based on his research and profuse study. Those range from philosophical musings to education, literature, social issues and feminism. He was also a regular columnist to several newspapers and those articles were not just fillers.

The Daily Star Books has published a collection of newspaper articles by Syed Abul Maksud under the title “Bangali Musalmaner Buddhibrittik Bibhrom O Biswashinota” in 2019. Some of the articles of the book are about the crème de la crème of the Bengali intellectuals and their sometimes deliberate and intentional contradictory behaviour. Such a revealing book is rare in Bangladesh.

In several cases, he was the first person to write books on the subjects he dealt with. His book on Sir Philip Joseph Hartog is one of such books. He also wrote a large book on Maulana Bhashani, who was one of the first persons from the then East Pakistan to say goodbye to West Pakistani rulers before the Liberation War in 1971.

Some of the articles of the book are about the crème de la crème of the Bengali intellectuals and their sometimes deliberate and intentional contradictory behaviour. Such a revealing book is rare in Bangladesh.

But he was not just a man of letters; he was an upright and a man of words too. He was a news editor at the state-run news agency, Bangladesh Sangbad Sangsatha (BSS) in 2004. At that time he wrote a scathing article in a newspaper on the attack on writer and Dhaka University professor Humayun Azad. The article invoked the ire of the then information minister and the prime minister’s political affairs adviser. They advised Syed Abul Maksud not to publish such columns. In protest, he resigned from the news agency job in just 15 minutes of receiving the “advice”. Later, he wrote, “If I were to choose between writing and a job, I would love to always choose the first one.”

23 October 2026 was the 80th birthday of Syed Abul Maksud, who breathed his last in 2021. A few newspaper articles were published by a handful of newspapers commemorating his birthday. But it passed mostly silently. It was not so unexpected though. But it would be better for us if we remember him and study his writings. They surely will help us in times like today.

item.title: ‘Honey trap’ gang lures wealthy men into rooms, then blackmails them
item.description:
The scheme began with introductions on social media, where the suspects gradually built fake romantic relationships with their targets before luring them to designated apartments or hotel rooms.

Other gang members would be waiting there. They would then intimidate the victims, hold them hostage and physically assault them. The gang would record compromising photos and videos and extort money by threatening to make the material public.

The Wari division of the Detective Branch (DB) of Dhaka Metropolitan Police has arrested five members of a suspected gang accused of extorting money through blackmail using this so-called “honey trap” scheme. They were arrested during a raid on a residential building in the capital’s Turag area on Saturday.

Dhaka Metropolitan Police disclosed the information in a press release on Sunday.

The arrestees are Abdur Rahman, 38; Pritam Biswas, also known as Anik Sheikh, 30; Arthojeet Bhakta, also known as Siddhartha, 20; Sabrin Kabir Prema, also known as Neha, 22; and Sadia Yasmin, also known as Mahi, 21.

According to police, Abdur Rahman is the alleged ringleader. Five mobile phones, three blank cheques and a torture belt were recovered from their possession.

Sources in the DB’s Wari division said the gang’s female members used fake identities on social media to establish romantic relationships with financially well-off men, including middle-aged and older businessmen.

They would then lure the men to designated apartments or hotel rooms.
There, the gang’s male members would hold the victims hostage, intimidate them and subject them to physical abuse. They would then extort money by threatening to publish compromising photos and videos. Even after paying once, the victims would not be left alone.

During the preliminary investigation, police learned that the gang members would demand additional payments through further blackmail.

According to police, the suspects frequently changed their residences and hideouts to evade law enforcement. They also used SIM cards registered under fake names and social media accounts created with false identities.

The DMP has urged people to exercise caution when using social media and to inform the police promptly if they fall victim to fraud or blackmail.

item.title: Biman extends suspension of Dammam, Riyadh flights until November 4
item.description:
Biman Bangladesh Airlines has extended the suspension of all flights on the Dhaka-Dammam and Dhaka-Riyadh routes until November 4 amid airport attacks in Saudi Arabia.
The airline’s public relations department announced the decision in a statement on Sunday evening.
According to the statement, passengers can use Jeddah and Medina international airports to travel to and from Saudi Arabia in emergencies.
Considering passenger demand, Biman has been operating 2 daily flights on the Dhaka-Jeddah route since October 16. The service will continue until November 4, the statement added.
Meanwhile, regular flights on the Dhaka-Medina route are being operated using Boeing 787 aircraft.
Biman authorities said they would provide updates on future flight operations and travel schedules in due course.
Passengers have been requested to contact their nearest Biman Bangladesh Airlines sales center for information about tickets and travel.

item.title: PM to leave for Japan tonight on a four-day official visit
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman is set to leave for Japan on Sunday for a four-day official visit at the invitation of his Japanese counterpart Sanae Takaichi.
During the visit, he will hold high-level bilateral talks with Takaichi, meet representatives of major Japanese companies and development institutions, visit industrial and energy facilities, and deliver the keynote address at the Japan-Bangladesh Economic Forum.
The prime minister will hold bilateral talks with Takaichi at her office on October 27, Foreign Secretary Asad Alam Siam told journalists at a curtain-raiser media briefing at the Foreign Ministry on October 20.
Takaichi will also host a luncheon in honor of the Bangladesh Prime Minister, he said.
The premier’s visit is expected to deepen the existing strategic partnership, attract fresh Japanese investment, expand trade and accelerate ongoing development projects, he added.
Discussions will focus on the effective implementation of the Bangladesh-Japan Economic Partnership Agreement (EPA), signed in February 2026, expanding access for Bangladeshi products to the Japanese market and strengthening business engagement.
The two sides will also explore wider cooperation in renewable energy, agriculture, science and technology, digital transformation, skills development and human resource development.
The prime minister is scheduled to deliver the keynote address at the Japan-Bangladesh Economic Forum and meet Japanese business leaders.
His tentative program includes engagements with the Japan-Bangladesh Parliamentary Friendship League and the chairman of the Japan-Bangladesh Committee for Commercial and Economic Cooperation.
Meetings are also being planned with the president of the Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA), the governor of the Japan Bank for International Cooperation (JBIC), the president of the Japan External Trade Organization (JETRO) and the chairman of the Sasakawa Peace Foundation.
The proposed itinerary includes visits to an LNG terminal and power plant in Futtsu City, Chiba; the headquarters of UNIQLO; and a Toyota factory in Nagoya.
The foreign secretary said the two sides were discussing draft memoranda of understanding and cooperation agreements covering agriculture, fisheries, human resource development, skills enhancement, civil aviation, trade, environmental conservation and local government modernization.
“We hope that many of these MoUs will be signed during the visit,” he said.
Around eight MoUs are under discussion, of which three to four could be signed during the visit. Separate agreements are also being pursued in education and human resource development.
Detailed discussions are planned on Japanese support for establishing factories in Bangladesh, generating employment and developing human resources in line with the prime minister’s priorities.
The two sides are also expected to discuss regional and international peace and stability, a sustainable and peaceful solution to the Rohingya crisis, stronger cooperation in addressing the energy crisis, and efforts to end international conflicts.
The visit follows the prime minister’s participation in an online meeting in April at the invitation of the Japanese premier, during which Bangladesh welcomed a Japan-led initiative to address energy challenges across Asia.
Japan has been a major development partner of Bangladesh since the establishment of diplomatic relations in 1972. Japanese assistance has supported major infrastructure projects, including the Dhaka metro rail, the third terminal of Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport and infrastructure development in Matarbari.
Shaheed President Ziaur Rahman visited Japan in 1978 and 1980, while former Prime Minister Khaleda Zia visited the country in 1994 and 2005.

item.title: Nahid accuses BNP of striking a 'secret deal' with India
item.description:
Opposition Chief Whip and National Citizen Party (NCP) Convener Nahid Islam on Sunday accused the government of striking a secret deal with India to destabilize the country’s hill regions.
“The BNP came to power by striking a deal with India. Now it is destabilizing the hills in the same way,” Nahid said at a public outreach program in Mirpur-10 in the afternoon.
Nahid alleged that BNP is maintaining a clandestine relationship with India, which he said is fuelling unrest in the hills and killing people along the border to put pressure on Bangladesh.
“Whenever India wants to pressurize Bangladesh, it creates unrest through hill separatists, shoots people dead at the border, or else opens the sluice gates of some rivers,” he said.
Expressing concern over the future of the Ganges water-sharing treaty, the NCP chief said: “We do not know what the government is thinking about the Ganges treaty. We have serious doubts about what kind of deal they will make with India.”
Terming the government “illegitimate”, Nahid said it was refraining from implementing the referendum decision in defiance of the people’s verdict.
“We wanted a radical overhaul of the constitution, but the government is amending it instead. They should remember that any future government can declare this amendment illegal at any time,” he said.
He also claimed that by not enforcing the referendum verdict, the government is lending legitimacy to the Awami League.
“The Awami League’s 10th, 11th and 12th parliaments are still legally valid. By not implementing the referendum, the Awami League is gaining legitimacy for its previous rule. Yet it is BNP that had been calling the Awami League illegitimate for years,” he said.
Nahid said his party feared the Awami League would be rehabilitated at the BNP’s hands, with the BNP voluntarily creating space for it to return to politics.
Launching a sharp attack on State Minister for Local Government Mir Shahe Alam, Nahid alleged that he became a minister under Tarique Rahman’s “friend quota” and had since established a “fiefdom” in his own constituency.
“He is now announcing mayoral candidates himself, which is completely illegal,” Nahid said.
He also claimed that the current city corporation administrators could not take part in the upcoming local government elections in any way, and all those now serving as administrators are illegitimate.

item.title: Saint Martin’s Island to reopen to tourists on November 1
item.description:
Saint Martin’s Island will reopen to tourists on November 1 after a nine-month closure aimed at protecting its fragile ecosystem and biodiversity.
The Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change issued an order to this effect on Sunday.
The island has remained closed to tourists since February 1 under a government decision to conserve its environment.
The decision to reopen the island was taken at an inter-ministerial meeting held at the Secretariat on October 12 to discuss tourist access to Saint Martin’s.
Following the meeting, Environment, Forest and Climate Change Minister Abdul Awal Mintoo said the government had decided to review the duration of tourists’ visits and stays, the daily tourist limit and the departure points for tourist vessels.
He said the government would make fresh decisions considering environmental and biodiversity conservation alongside tourists’ safety and ease of access. Existing restrictions would remain in force until new directives were issued, he added.
Under the latest order, the island will remain open to tourists until March 15, 2027, during the current tourist season.

item.title: NCP dissolves women’s wing committee, names 3-member convening panel
item.description:
National Citizen Party (NCP) on Sunday dissolved the committee of its women’s wing, Jatiya Nari Shakti, and replaced it with a new three-member convening committee, tasking it with forming a full committee within 15 days.
In a statement, the party said Mahmuda Alam Mitu, a lawmaker on a reserved women’s seat in Parliament, has been made convener of the new committee.
Nusrat Tabassum, another reserved-seat MP, has been appointed member secretary, while Monjila Jhuma has been given the responsibility of chief organizer.
The party said the committee was formed on the “directive” of NCP Convener Nahid Islam and Member Secretary Akhtar Hossen.
According to the statement, the convening committee must form a full-fledged committee within the next 15 days.
The last full convening committee of the NCP’s affiliated body was announced in April this year.
The 53-member panel was headed by NCP Joint Convener Monira Sharmin as convener. Mitu, who has now been named convener, served as member secretary of that committee.

item.title: Five held over honey-trapping, blackmailing wealthy men in Dhaka
item.description:
The Detective Branch (DB) of Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) has arrested five alleged members of a honey-trapping and blackmailing gang, including its suspected ringleader, in the capital’s Turag area.
The gang allegedly used fake social media identities to lure wealthy middle-aged and elderly men into romantic relationships before inviting them to designated apartments or hotel rooms, where they were held hostage and blackmailed with compromising photos and videos to extort money.
DB chief Shafiqul Islam disclosed the information at a press briefing on Sunday afternoon.
The arrestees are Jit Bhakta alias Abdur Rahman, 38; Pritam Biswas alias Anik Sheikh, 30; Arthajit Bhakta alias Siddhartha, 20; Sabrin Kabir Prema alias Neha, 22; and Sadia Yasmin alias Mahi, 21. The group comprises three men and two women.
According to the DB’s Wari Division, Jit Bhakta, also known as Abdur Rahman, is the alleged ringleader.
The gang’s female members allegedly developed romantic relationships with wealthy men, including businessmen, through fake social media profiles before luring them to designated apartments or hotel rooms.
There, the male members allegedly held the victims hostage, threatened them and subjected them to physical abuse. They also recorded compromising photos and videos and threatened to release the footage unless the victims paid money.
Preliminary investigations suggest that the gang continued to extort money even after receiving initial payments, repeatedly threatening to expose the footage, police said.
To evade law enforcement, the suspects allegedly changed their residences and hideouts frequently and used SIM cards registered under false identities and fake social media accounts.
Acting on intelligence and using technological assistance, a DB team from the Wari Division tracked down the suspects and raided a residential building in Turag, arresting all five.
Police recovered five mobile phones, three blank cheques and a torture belt from their possession.
A case has been filed against the accused, and further legal proceedings are underway.
The DMP urged residents to exercise caution when using social media and to promptly inform police if they fall victim to fraud or blackmail. It also said surveillance and operations against such crimes would continue.

item.title: 3 jailed for life over rape on moving bus
item.description:
A court in Tangail has sentenced three men, including a bus driver and his assistant, to life imprisonment for raping a female passenger on a moving bus on the Dhaka-Tangail highway on January 14.
Tangail Women and Children Repression Prevention Tribunal Judge ANM Ilias delivered the verdict on Sunday afternoon. The convicts were also fined Tk2 lakh each, with an additional year of simple imprisonment if they fail to pay.
The convicts are bus driver Md Altaf, 25, son of Abdur Rob of Nanderai village in Chirirbandar upazila, Dinajpur; his assistant Md Robbi, 21, son of Khokon Mia of Shibpur village in Jamalganj upazila, Sunamganj; and bus conductor Sagar alias Sajib Matubbar, 24, son of Chunnu Matubbar of Chandar Hat Bazar in Nagarkanda upazila, Faridpur.
Public Prosecutor Omaraw Khan Dipu of the tribunal said the woman boarded a Savar Paribahan bus from Dhaka at around 11:45pm on January 14, intending to travel to Ashulia.
Other passengers got off at various stops along the way. The three men then allegedly raped her in succession on the moving bus. They also threatened her and took her earrings, Tk36,000 in cash and a mobile phone before driving around the Dhaka-Tangail highway.
The following day, the bus stopped near the Kortia underpass in Tangail Sadar upazila. The woman reported the incident to highway police patrolling the area.
Highway police later handed the bus and the three accused over to Tangail Sadar police. The woman filed a rape case against them at Tangail Sadar police station that day.
Inspector (Investigation) Victor Banerjee of Tangail Sadar police station investigated the case and submitted a charge sheet to the court on April 29.
After recording testimony from 15 witnesses, the court delivered its verdict. The convicts were subsequently sent to Tangail District Jail.

item.title: Sahadat Hossain now made CCC administrator
item.description:
The government has now appointed BNP leader Dr Sahadat Hossain, who became the mayor of Chittagong City Corporation (CCC) following a court verdict, as the full-time administrator of the same city corporation.
The Local Government Division issued a notification on Sunday in this regard.
According to the notification, he will remain in the position until the city corporation is constituted or until further orders are issued.
He will exercise the powers and perform the duties of the city corporation's mayor under Section 4(3) of the Local Government (City Corporation) Amendment Act, 2026.
Sahadat will receive a monthly honorarium and other allowances as prescribed by the rules, the notification added.
Sahadat had filed a case seeking cancellation of the results of the CCC election held on January 27, 2021.
On October 1, 2024, a Chittagong court declared him the winner of the election after hearing his case.
On August 19, 2024, the interim government removed then CCC Mayor Rezaul Karim Chowdhury after the fall of the Awami League government on August 5 in the face of a mass upsurge.
Later, Divisional Commissioner Tofayel Islam was appointed as the CCC administrator.

item.title: Dynamic City Lions Club, Salma-Adil Foundation holds eye camp & rehabilitation program in Banshkhali
item.description:
More than 600 villagers received healthcare services, rehabilitation assistance and support through a day-long community program organized at Banshkhali Hamedia Rahima Fazil Madrasha in Chittagong.
The program was organized by Lions Club of Chittagong Dynamic City and Leo Club of Chittagong Golden City, under Lions District 315 B4, with support from the Salma-Adil Foundation.
The program included an eye care camp, tree plantation, health awareness activities and rehabilitation assistance for underprivileged families.
The eye care camp provided primary eye treatment, identification of patients requiring cataract surgery, blood group testing, diabetes screening and distribution of spectacles.
Lions Charitable Eye Institute and Hospital, Chittagong, supported the delivery of eye care services.
Awareness activities were also conducted on childhood cancer, dengue, chikungunya and scabies, alongside tree plantation initiatives.
As part of the rehabilitation program, assistance was provided to vulnerable families through house construction, distribution of livestock to support livelihoods, sewing machines for self-employment, and corrugated iron sheets to help repair and rebuild homes.
Financial assistance was also provided for the marriages of daughters from underprivileged families.
To support religious education, copies of the Holy Quran, turbans for Hafez and rehal were distributed.
The program was held under the leadership of Lion Salma Adil, MJF, president of Lions Club of Chittagong Dynamic City for the current service year along with the chairman of Salma Adil Foundation Ziauddin Adil.
Additionally, Lion Afroza Begum, club service chairperson, provided overall supervision.
Lion Mohammad Kamruzzaman Liton, PMJF, governor of Lions District 315 B4, attended as the chief guest.
Lion Mohammad Abu Bakar Siddique, PMJF, first vice district governor, was special guest, while former district governor Lion Sheikh Shamsuddin Ahmed Siddique, PMJF, attended as distinguished guest.
Lion Mohammad Kamruzzaman Liton said: “Lions are continuously working for the welfare of people around the world. The coordinated service initiative by Lions Club of Chittagong Dynamic City and the Salma-Adil Foundation is commendable. Such activities will inspire others to come forward in humanitarian service.”
Lion Salma Adil said: “Our goal is to make underprivileged people self-reliant by meeting their basic needs, ensuring access to healthcare, and creating opportunities for housing and livelihoods. We want to continue such activities to help people build dignified lives.”
Among those present were Lions District Cabinet treasurer Lion Zillur Rahman, MJF; GST Lion Helal Uddin; GLT Lion Muhammad Musa; Lion Sabbir Ahmed; Lion Mahi Chowdhury; Lion Arshadur Rahman; Lion AKM Salauddin, MJF; Lion Nurul Alam; Lion Ziauddin Sohel; Zone Chairperson 1 Lion Saiful Islam; Lion Jahangir Alam; Lion Abdur Razzak; Lion M A Aziz Howlader; Lion Saiful Islam; and Leo Ariful Islam.
Presidents, secretaries and other district-level leaders of Lions and Leo Clubs also attended the program.
The event was hosted by Lion Shawkat Chowdhury, MJF.

item.title: Mobile billing expands digital payment options for users
item.description:
Mobile phone users of Robi Axiata and Banglalink can now use their mobile balances to purchase a wider range of eligible products and services, as the Bangladesh Telecommunication Regulatory Commission (BTRC) has raised transaction limits under Direct Operator Billing (DOB).
The revised limits allow customers to spend up to Tk5,000 a month and Tk50,000 a year through their mobile operator accounts, expanding the scope of a payment channel that offers an alternative to bank accounts and credit cards for eligible digital purchases.
The approval will remain effective for six months from July 20, 2026, bringing Robi and Banglalink under the higher limits previously approved for Grameenphone.
According to BTRC documents, the commission granted retrospective approval for the revised limits, subject to conditions outlined in a letter sent to the two operators on September 13.
Robi and Banglalink applied for the increase on August 25.
The commission said extending the higher limits to both operators was necessary to ensure fair competition, as allowing only Grameenphone to offer the facility could give it an undue advantage, despite its status as a “significant market power operator”.
Robi welcomed the initiative by the Bangladesh Bank and the BTRC to increase the Direct Operator Billing (DOB) limit.
Talking to BSS, Shahed Alam, chief corporate and regulatory officer at Robi Axiata, said: “We believe this will accelerate digital inclusion, promote digital transactions, support the transition to a cashless society, and expand customers’ access to alternative payment methods and digital services.”
DOB enables customers to pay for specified products and services directly from their mobile balances.
Under the revised limits, eligible purchases include smartphones and SIM-based modems and routers, either through outright payments or instalments, alongside other permitted digital products and services.
However, the increased limits do not allow mobile balances to be used as unrestricted digital money.
The service remains subject to regulatory safeguards and restrictions on the types of transactions permitted.
Operators must comply with applicable Bangladesh Bank instructions and obtain approval under the revised guidelines for prepaid payment instruments once they are issued.
They must also comply with the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2024, the Money Laundering Prevention Act, 2012, and the Anti-Terrorism Act, 2009.
Customers must complete know-your-customer (KYC) procedures in line with Bangladesh Financial Intelligence Unit requirements before using the service.
The rules prohibit DOB payments for virtual currencies used in social media applications and games, including coins, points, credits, coupons, diamonds and gems.
Payments to applications that collect public investments, provide loans, store money or facilitate financial transactions are also prohibited.
The service cannot be used for gambling, casino activities, lotteries, cryptocurrency or crypto-asset trading, foreign-exchange trading, stock-market trading or multi-level marketing.
Where payments to non-resident merchants require foreign-currency remittances, operators must obtain approval from the Bangladesh Bank's Foreign Exchange Policy Department, where applicable.
The BTRC has directed operators to ensure that customers receive the digital products and services they purchase, protect customer interests, and establish clear refund and chargeback policies.
DOB operations will remain subject to Bangladesh Bank inspections, while mobile network operators will be treated as reporting organizations under the relevant money-laundering and anti-terrorism laws.
The latest revision follows several changes to DOB spending limits since the service was introduced in Bangladesh in 2018, when customers could spend up to Tk600 a month and Tk3,000 a year.
In December 2025, Bangladesh Bank temporarily raised the limits to Tk2,000 a month and Tk20,000 a year, paving the way for the latest increase.

item.title: One-person company registrations on the rise
item.description:
The number of One-Person Company (OPC) registrations is on the rise in Bangladesh.
In FY26, 818 such companies were registered, representing a 235% increase compared to the previous fiscal.
In the first three months of the current FY27, an additional 376 companies have been registered.
However, the mandatory requirement of a minimum paid-up capital of Tk25 lakh is keeping many small entrepreneurs out of this structure.
Relevant officials and experts note that OPCs were introduced with the goals of easing business operations for sole entrepreneurs, bringing informal businesses into the formal economy, and boosting local and foreign investment.
Yet, high capital conditions and administrative complexities are limiting the potential of this initiative.
According to data from the Registrar of Joint Stock Companies and Firms (RJSC), 124 OPCs were registered in FY22, followed by 140 in FY23, 139 in FY24, and 244 in FY25.
That figure rose significantly to 818 in FY26.
During the July–September period of the current fiscal, 376 companies were registered.
The registration count for these three months alone is nearly 54% higher than that of the entire FY25.
In total, the number of OPC registrations in the country reached 1,841 as of September of the current fiscal year.
An RJSC official stated that the condition of having a minimum paid-up capital of Tk25 lakh is a major hurdle for entrepreneurs wishing to register an OPC.
Private limited companies with multiple owners face no such minimum capital obligation, whereas it remains mandatory for sole-proprietor companies.
He added that this capital disparity discourages micro-entrepreneurs and sole founders from forming an OPC.
To address this issue, the relevant ministry and the registrar's office have initiated efforts to amend the minimum paid-up capital provision.
One of the key objectives of launching OPCs was to attract foreign direct investment and simplify the process of starting a business.
However, procedural hurdles such as opening bank accounts, bringing capital into the country, and obtaining required approvals remain significant barriers for foreign entrepreneurs.
According to experts, alongside relaxing capital requirements, it is essential to simplify the registration process and raise awareness among entrepreneurs about OPC-related laws and regulations.
Otherwise, despite the increase in registrations, the full potential of this corporate structure to engage small entrepreneurs and draw investment will remain unfulfilled.

item.title: Hotels, resorts can retain 15% forex earnings from foreigners
item.description:
Commercial establishments—including hotels, resorts, restaurants, and shopping malls—can retain up to 15% of foreign currency earned from foreign tourists and shoppers via international cards in their Foreign Currency (FC) accounts.
The remaining amount must be encashed into Bangladeshi Taka according to regulations.
The Foreign Exchange Policy Department (FEPD) of Bangladesh Bank issued a circular in this regard on Sunday (October 25).
The instructions have been sent to all Authorized Dealer (AD) banks across the country.
According to the circular, a maximum of 15% of foreign currency earned against the sale of goods and services to foreign tourists and buyers through international cards or approved payment systems can be deposited into the respective business's FC account.
The remaining balance must be converted into Taka following standard rules.
Funds deposited in the FC account can be used for legitimate foreign currency transactions via international cards and for paying applicable VAT and taxes.
In addition to maintaining proper infrastructure to accept international cards, the relevant establishments must strictly comply with directives regarding Anti-Money Laundering and Countering the Financing of Terrorism (AML/CFT), as well as Know Your Customer (KYC) guidelines.
The central bank hopes that this initiative will make it easier to receive foreign currency from foreign tourists and buyers and use it to conduct legitimate international transactions.

item.title: Abbasi receives legal notice over derogatory remarks on journalists
item.description:
A legal notice has been sent to Islamic preacher Mufti Dr Syed Muhammad Enayetullah Abbasi, demanding an unconditional apology within seven days for his derogatory remarks about journalists and alleged threats to beat them.
Supreme Court lawyer Khademul Islam issued the notice on Sunday on behalf of Azharul Islam Sujon, an executive committee member of the Court Reporters Unity, an organisation of journalists covering lower courts.
Advocate Khademul Islam confirmed the matter, saying legal action would be taken if Abbasi failed to withdraw his remarks and apologise within seven days of receiving the notice.
The notice said Abbasi made the remarks at an annual religious sermon and prayer gathering at Nishchintapur Hafizia Madrasa in Matlab upazila of Chandpur on October 19.
During the event, he reportedly described Bangladeshi journalists as the worst and said they should be “beaten like dogs”.
He also accused journalists of practising yellow journalism, failing to report positively on a state minister’s alleged efforts to dismantle a drug syndicate, and receiving funding from foreign intelligence agencies. He further alleged that they did not want Bangladesh to prosper.
According to the notice, the remarks amounted to defamatory statements, threats of assault and incitement, creating an atmosphere of fear and insecurity for journalists.
The notice warned that legal action would be pursued under applicable laws if Abbasi failed to comply with the demand for an apology.

item.title: Police made 1,314 arrests in France’s protests
item.description:
Police arrested 1,314 people in weekend protests across France, the interior ministry said Sunday, adding that 53 officers were hurt in clashes.
The arrests occurred as violence broke out on the margins of mass demonstrations in major cities on Saturday over the high cost of living.
It was the second consecutive weekend of unrest in France, which is heading to presidential elections in April and May to choose a successor to Emmanuel Macron, who is reaching his two-term limit.
The interior ministry said police responded to 75 fires during Saturday’s protests, adding that 24 shops were looted.
“Several investigations have been opened,” it said in a statement, without giving details. It said that the rest of Saturday night, after the clashes had died down, was “calm.”
The ministry statement on Sunday did not say how many protesters were hurt.
Late Saturday, Interior Minister Laurent Nunez spoke of two serious injuries among protesters: one in Toulouse and one in Clermont-Ferrand.
The Toulouse prefecture, which reports to the interior ministry, told AFP that a 20-year-old man was seriously hurt with a wound to his hand.
A street medic who tended demonstrators told AFP, on condition of anonymity, that the man had “several fingers” blown off his right hand.
The prefecture covering Clermont-Ferrand said a man there also had a hand hurt, but did not suffer the loss of any fingers.
A French regional daily, La Nouvelle Republique, reported that a man in Poitiers was hurt in his left eye, showing a photo of a man holding his face.
The newspaper’s photographer told AFP he was a 19-year-old who was wounded during a charge by riot police firing stun grenades and tear gas.
There have been several instances in recent weeks, during student protests in France, of people being maimed by police stun grenades or tear gas grenades.
It was not known if the injuries reported from Saturday were from those police weapons. Officials said investigations had been opened in at least some of the cases.

item.title: Yemen’s Houthis target Saudi Arabia’s south as Riyadh airport due to reopen
item.description:
Yemen’s Houthis launched wide-ranging strikes across swathes of southern Saudi Arabia on Sunday, as the kingdom announced the partial reopening of Riyadh international airport despite repeated attacks by the group.
Alerts warning of possible attacks were activated across the kingdom’s south throughout the day, with the Saudi-led military coalition fighting the Houthis saying at least 10 ballistic missiles were intercepted.
Saudi Arabia, which leads a military coalition fighting the Iran-backed Houthis, has faced a barrage of strikes from the group in recent weeks.
The fighting erupted after a years-long truce between the Houthis and Yemen’s Riyadh-backed government fell apart.
“The bombardment has been very heavy since this morning -- may God keep us safe. Everything is shaking because of the explosions,” one resident in Khamis Mushait told AFP Sunday on condition of anonymity.
Further north, Riyadh’s international airport said flights would resume on Sunday after a two-week closure following the Houthi strikes.
However it remained unclear to what extent the airport was operational.
The Houthi fighters have carried out waves of strikes on the airport, including an attack this month that killed 13 people and wounded more than 300, the deadliest in the kingdom in more than a decade.
The group has also targeted oil infrastructure and other sites.
Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree warned that Riyadh airport was still “unsafe” and a “military target.”
“The Yemeni Armed Forces warn all international, regional and local airlines -- as well as staff and travelers -- against using King Khalid Airport in Riyadh, as it is unsafe and serves as a military target for our forces,” he said.
“The Saudi regime shall bear the consequences of any operations at the airport.”
As the airport prepared to open, AFP journalists in Riyadh heard three explosions in the early hours of Sunday, with residents receiving alert messages for a “hostile aerial threat” urging them to stay in a safe place.
The warning came as the Saudi-led coalition fighting the Houthis said it had downed a ballistic missile launched by the group towards the capital, as well as two drones in the capital area.
“Air defenses intercepted and destroyed a ballistic missile launched by the terrorist Houthi militia toward Riyadh,” the coalition posted on X.
Later Sunday morning, the coalition said its forces intercepted a cruise missile fired by the Houthis at the kingdom’s southern city of Khamis Mushait.
Attacks appeared to target areas across the south, with warnings also issued for Abha city along with areas in Taif, Namas and Jazan.
The attacks came after the Houthi fighters said that -- in the space of 24 hours -- they targeted three Saudi airports, including in Riyadh, energy installations, a pipeline and an air base.
The Saudi civil defense agency said it had also responded to falling debris in the Mecca and Medina regions on Saturday after intercepting two Houthi missiles.
The Houthis denied targeting the cities, the two holiest in Islam, calling the Saudi claim a “huge lie.”
The Houthis also fired at the southern Yemeni city of Aden, the interim seat of the Saudi-backed government, saying they targeted a naval base and military camp overseen by Saudi forces.
The flare-up in Yemen, with the Houthis taking control of the entire Red Sea coast in a lightning offensive last month, has further destabilized the region and disrupted oil markets.
The Houthi attacks have dealt a blow to Saudi Arabia, the world’s biggest exporter of crude, disrupting businesses, airlines and residents, and rattling its drive to shift its international image.

item.title: Obama blasts Trump’s ‘chaos and cruelty’ while campaigning for Democrats
item.description:
Former US president Barack Obama delivered scathing criticisms of current leader Donald Trump at rallies Saturday in Ohio and Michigan to support Democratic candidates ahead of the November 3 midterm elections.
Democrats are attempting to wrest back control of one or both chambers of the US Congress, which are currently controlled by Trump’s Republican party.
Obama retains considerable popularity among the Democratic base, which he is keen to leverage to support his party’s candidates.
In both states, the 65-year-old former president blamed the Trump administration for the rising cost of living, a top voter concern.
“The current president chose to make a series of bad decisions,” Obama said in Cleveland, Ohio, where he rallied in support of former Democratic senator Sherrod Brown.
“Most importantly, he decided to start an unnecessary war that nobody asked for.”
The war on Iran has sent oil prices soaring as Tehran effectively blocked the Strait of Hormuz after being attacked.
“After two years of chaos and cruelty and corruption and incompetence, the likes of which we have not seen in the modern era, you get a chance to say, ‘Enough is enough,’ “Obama declared. “We are voting for change right here in Ohio.”
Later, in Michigan, Obama campaigned for Abdul El-Sayed, from the party’s left wing, who is in a close race with Republican Mike Rogers for the US Senate.
“Imagine the power duo of Abdul and Elissa,” Obama said, referring to the incumbent Democratic Senator Elissa Slotkin, who is not up for election this year.
“You got a Muslim man, you got a Jewish woman fighting for you in the United States Senate. That’s something, Michigan, you can be proud of.”
Trump slammed Obama’s campaign in Michigan in a post on Truth Social on Sunday, urging voters to choose Rogers.
“Obama was a grossly incompetent President! He paid off Iran with $Billions, and gave them a road to a Nuclear Weapon,” Trump said, referring to a 2015 deal negotiated under Obama that offered Iran sanctions relief in return for drastically scaling back its nuclear work.
Trump withdrew from that deal during his first term and imposed sweeping sanctions, including on countries that bought Iranian oil.
Western countries accuse Iran of seeking to acquire nuclear weapons, something Tehran denies, defending its right to what it insists is a civilian nuclear program.
Obama also urged voters to cast their ballots as soon as possible since early voting is already open in both states.
“Don’t procrastinate, don’t equivocate,” Obama said.
In Ohio, Brown will attempt a comeback against incumbent Republican Senator Jon Husted, while the race for governor will be contested between Democrat Amy Acton and Republican Vivek Ramaswamy, a former presidential candidate in 2024.
Polls for Ohio give Democrats a slight lead in both races, but the results are expected to be close.
Obama also took digs at Trump’s renovation projects across the US capital, including his botched renovation of the National Mall’s Reflecting Pool, his construction of a massive White House Ballroom and the gilded decorations he has adorned the Oval Office with during his second tenure.
“He’s got the White House looking like Saddam Hussein opened a Cheesecake Factory,” Obama said, referring to the popular but indulgent American restaurant chain.
Nationally, polls also suggest that Democrats could regain control of the House of Representatives but face a much more competitive contest for the Senate.

item.title: BUFT hosts national quiz competition 2.0, 2026
item.description:
BGMEA University of Fashion & Technology (BUFT) organized the “BGMEA Presents BUFT National Quiz Competition 2.0, 2026” on October 25 at its Abdullah Hil Rakib Auditorium.
The competition was powered by BRB, Nexagen and RFL, and co-powered by DESCO, Asutex, System Engineering Limited and OMC. The event was organized with support from the BUFT Brand Ambassador Team.
Md Mesbah Uddin Ali, chairman of the BUFT Board of Trustees and Wega Group, presided over the event, while S M Jahangir Hossain, member of parliament for Dhaka-18, attended as chief guest.
Mohammad Imtiaj, director of the Department of Public Relations, conducted the program. Prof Dr Md Abdul Jalil, dean of the Faculty of Sciences, delivered the welcome address, while BUFT Vice Chancellor Prof Dr Engr Ayub Nabi Khan also spoke.
A total of 1,424 college students from different parts of the country who qualified in the preliminary round participated in the competition.
Contestants took part in the second multiple-choice question (MCQ) round, from which 30 teams advanced to the quarter-finals. Six teams then competed in the buzzer round to secure places in the semi-finals, before 4 teams qualified for the grand finale, which featured audio-visual and rapid-fire rounds.
Dhaka Commerce College emerged as champion, while Birshreshtha Munshi Abdur Rouf Public College finished first runner-up and Zirabo Cantonment Public School and College finished second runner-up. Farik Hasan Omio of Dhaka Commerce College was named Best Contestant.
The event was attended by the acting pro-vice chancellor, registrar, deans, faculty members, parents, university officers, distinguished guests and senior journalists.
The competition concluded with an award ceremony, a group photo session and a cultural program and fashion runway organized with support from the BUFT Heritage Club and BUFT Cultural Club.
Channel 24 was the event partner, Learnup was the knowledge partner, and Shomoy TV, Daily Amader Shomoy, The Business Standard, The Daily Campus and Radio Today were the media partners.

item.title: Humaiun Kobir gets full ministerial authority to lead CHOGM
item.description:
State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir has been granted full Cabinet Minister-level authority to lead Bangladesh's delegation to the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting (CHOGM 2026) as acting foreign minister.
The summit is scheduled to be held in Antigua and Barbuda from November 1 to 4, according to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
A notification issued by the Cabinet Division today said Kobir had been conferred with full authority equivalent to that of a Cabinet Minister under Clause 4(iii) of the Rules of Business, 1996.
The authority has been granted specifically for leading the Bangladesh delegation at CHOGM 2026 and discharging the duties of the Foreign Minister as Acting Foreign Minister during the high-level gathering.
The notification was issued by order of the president and signed by Cabinet Secretary Nasimul Ghani.
Under the arrangement, Kobir will represent Bangladesh at the Commonwealth summit with full ministerial authority, enabling him to lead the country's delegation in his capacity as Acting Foreign Minister.

item.title: Ishraque’s rifle was licensed in his name, carried by aide
item.description:
A rifle carried by former Chhatra Dal leader Pavel Sikder during an anti-drug operation led by former State Minister for Liberation War Affairs Ishraque Hossain was licensed in Ishraque’s name, the Detective Branch (DB) chief has said, raising questions about the use of licensed firearms by people other than their registered owners.
DB chief Shafiqul Islam, an additional commissioner of Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP), told Dhaka Tribune that the investigation had found that the two firearms seen in the hands of Ishraque and Pavel were licensed.
Asked whether one person could use a rifle licensed to another person, Shafiqul said those involved had been warned for the first time. If such an incident occurred again, action would be taken under the law.
“We have informed them and made it clear that these licensed firearms may only be used by the individual for their own protection,” he said.
The incident took place on October 17, when Ishraque visited the Dayaganj Ghuntighar railway gate area near Gandaria railway station in Dhaka during an anti-drug operation, carrying a pistol. Pavel, the former convener of Dhaka Metropolitan South Chhatra Dal, was seen carrying a rifle identified by DB authorities as a Colt M4 Carbine, .22 Long Rifle calibre semi-automatic carbine, bearing serial number BP060322 and manufactured by Carl Walther in Germany.
After a video of the incident went viral on social media, Ishraque resigned on the prime minister’s instructions. Images and videos showing firearms being openly displayed in broad daylight during the operation triggered widespread debate over the legality of their use and the political implications of the incident.
DMP has ordered an investigation into the display of firearms by Ishraque and his associates during the operation. The deputy commissioner of DMP’s Wari Division has been assigned to investigate the incident.
According to DB sources, investigators have been instructed to verify the incident and establish the source and legality of the firearms. They have been asked to determine whether the weapons were firearms lost by the military, illegal weapons smuggled into the country or legally owned firearms used in violation of regulations. Sources also said ballistic and forensic opinions were being sought.
At a press conference at the Press Club following the incident, Ishraque said the firearm he carried during the operation was licensed in his own name. He also said he had asked a colleague to keep the second firearm for security reasons.
Jaber Md Shoaib, additional deputy commissioner at the Dhaka Deputy Commissioner’s Office, told Dhaka Tribune on Sunday afternoon that the licences for both firearms had been issued by the DC office. He confirmed that the rifle carried by Pavel was also licensed in Ishraque’s name.
Shoaib said the licences for both firearms had been obtained in accordance with the rules and that no regulations had been violated.
According to the Ministry of Home Affairs’ firearms licensing policy, licensed firearms are intended to be used only when absolutely necessary to protect the life of the licence holder or their family. Displaying firearms in public in a manner that causes fear among others is prohibited. Civilians cannot independently conduct operations using licensed firearms in this manner without the presence of law enforcement agencies.
Lawyers say that even if a firearm is legally owned, carrying or using it in circumstances that breach the licence conditions could constitute a violation. Whether any conditions were breached will depend on an investigation and an examination of the relevant documents.
Supreme Court lawyer Humayun Kabir told Dhaka Tribune: “Even a licensed firearm can only be used to protect one’s own life. However, in the incident involving Ishraque Saheb, I did not see any threat to the lives of those who used the firearms. Using firearms openly in this manner is harmful to the government and the state. Law enforcement agencies must take action in this regard.”
The public display of firearms by political leaders in the capital has raised concerns among local residents. Concerned citizens have called for the findings of an investigation into those seen carrying firearms in the videos, including Pavel, to be made public.
Niakat Ali, a Gandaria resident and former government employee, told Dhaka Tribune on Monday afternoon: “Using firearms openly in this manner creates fear among ordinary people. The police could have assisted in the anti-drug operation. Ishraque could have been present and provided support. Moreover, the rifle we saw in Pavel’s hands needs to be identified again. Weapons of this type were seen during the July movement. The government should take action on this matter.”
Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami Secretary General Mia Golam Parwar told Dhaka Tribune on Wednesday afternoon: “Even if a firearm is licensed, there are rules governing its use. The government should take action against those violating these rules. If the government shows weakness in this matter, it will send a very bad message. It will also encourage criminals.”
A video of the incident was posted on Ishraque’s Facebook page and quickly went viral, prompting widespread discussion. Another video showed the detained individuals being handed over to the police. Ishraque could be seen holding a pistol, while two other people accompanying him were also seen carrying firearms.
Ishraque was accompanied by two personal bodyguards he had appointed, Tofazzal Hossain and Lavlu. A government bodyguard was also present. The bodyguards appointed by Ishraque were carrying firearms, while the government bodyguard was seen pointing a firearm.

item.title: 100 sued over police attack in Gopalganj, 7 arrested
item.description:
A case has been filed against 100 people over an attack on police and vandalism of a police vehicle in Gopalganj, with 40 named and 60 unidentified accused.
Seven people arrested in connection with the incident were shown arrested in the case and sent to jail by a court order on Sunday.
Police said Sub-Inspector Md Ful Mia of Gopalganj Sadar Police Station filed the case on Sunday afternoon over an attack on police, assault and vehicle vandalism allegedly carried out while chanting “Joy Bangla”.
The seven accused were sent to Gopalganj court after initial questioning. The court subsequently ordered their transfer to jail.
Gopalganj Sadar Police Station Officer-in-Charge Md Aminul Islam said leaders and activists of the banned Chhatra League and Jubo League staged a flash procession on Saturday in support of former prime minister Sheikh Hasina, chanting “Joy Bangla”.
A police patrol team encountered the procession in the Burimar Gachtala area of Raghunathpur in Sadar upazila. When police tried to stop the march, the participants allegedly attacked officers with sticks and locally made weapons and vandalised a police pickup van.
Sub-Inspector Ful Mia and another police officer were injured in the attack, the OC said.
The seven arrested have been sent to jail by court order, while efforts are underway to arrest others involved in the incident, he added.

item.title: Mass media campaign for front-of-package warning labels on packaged foods launched
item.description:
A mass media campaign to raise public awareness and support for front-of-package warning labels on high-sugar, high-salt, and high-saturated-fat packaged foods and drinks was launched in Dhaka on Sunday.
The campaign aims to support government efforts to introduce warning labels that help consumers identify unhealthy products that may harm their health.
The campaign, named the FOPL Campaign, was launched at a press conference at the National Press Club on Sunday. It is jointly organized by the Coalition for Healthy Food, the Center for Law and Policy Affairs (CLPA), Dhaka Ahsania Mission (DAM), the National Heart Foundation (NHF), PROGGA and Work for a Better Bangladesh (WBB) Trust.
The initiative comes amid a growing burden of diet-related noncommunicable diseases (NCDs) in Bangladesh. NCDs account for nearly 71% of all deaths in the country, with cardiovascular disease and Type 2 diabetes among the leading causes. Overweight prevalence among adults is approximately 31.8%, while 13.4% are living with obesity. Overweight and obesity increase the risk of NCDs, including Type 2 diabetes, cardiovascular disease and stroke.
Front-of-package warning labels help consumers quickly identify packaged foods and drinks containing excessive amounts of sugar, salt and saturated fat. By making nutritional information clearer and easier to understand, the labels can help people make informed choices and discourage purchases of unhealthy products. They are considered an evidence-based policy tool to improve food environments and reduce diet-related diseases.
Bangladesh Food Safety Authority (BFSA) Chairman Md Safiqul Islam, an additional secretary, attended the launch as chief guest and formally inaugurated the campaign.
The event was chaired by Dr Sohel Reza Choudhury, professor and head of research and epidemiology at NHF, and moderated by Iqbal Masud, director of the health and WASH sector at DAM.
Professor Dr Mohammad Shoeb, BFSA member for food industry and production, and Muhammad Ruhul Quddus, Bangladesh country lead at Global Health Advocacy Incubator (GHAI), attended as special guests. Saifuddin Ahmed, executive director of WBB Trust; ABM Zubair, executive director of PROGGA; and Advocate Syed Mahbubul Alam, secretary of CLPA, were also present.
Safiqul Islam said ensuring food safety remained one of the authority’s key priorities. The BFSA was working to formulate the necessary regulations on front-of-package warning labels to raise awareness of unhealthy packaged foods and beverages high in sugar, salt and saturated fat, he said.
The two-month campaign will run until December 13, 2026, across television and radio, digital platforms, social media, online and print newspapers, and Google advertising.
The campaign will highlight unhealthy ingredients and excessive levels of sugar, salt and saturated fat in commonly consumed packaged products. It will also support the government in introducing regulations on front-of-package warning labels for packaged foods and drinks in Bangladesh.
Campaign materials include video and audio commercials, static images and other public-facing content, which will also be shared through partner organisations’ social media pages.

item.title: Media stakeholders call for action on media reform commission recommendations
item.description:
News media stakeholders have called for coordinated action to advance policy discussions and implement the recommendations of the Media Reform Commission, emphasizing the need for comprehensive structural reform to protect editorial independence, ensure journalists’ professional and financial security, and restore audience trust.
They also stressed the importance of strengthening self-regulatory mechanisms within news outlets, including adherence to editorial policies, transparent and accountable management systems, and accessible grievance redress mechanisms for audiences.
The observations emerged at a divisional consultation held in Chittagong on Sunday, organized by the Media Resources Development Initiative (MRDI) to discuss ways to improve the professional and ethical standards of journalism in Bangladesh and assess a viable framework for effective media self-regulation.
The consultation was the fourth in MRDI’s series of divisional consultations, following those in Khulna, Barisal and Sylhet. It was held under the Canada Fund for Local Initiatives (CFLI), with funding from the High Commission of Canada in Bangladesh.
News media owners and publishers, editors, news managers and gatekeepers, leaders of journalist unions and associations, university teachers, and civil society representatives from Chittagong and other districts of the division took part in the discussion.
In his opening presentation, MRDI Executive Director Hasibur Rahman said that more effective self-regulation would leave less scope for external interference in the news media. He added that strengthening the media’s own accountability mechanisms was essential to protecting press freedom.
“Press freedom depends on the trust of the audience. As long as readers, listeners and viewers have trust in the news media, they will be able to enjoy that freedom. To maintain this trust, news outlets must establish their own accountability mechanisms,” he said.
Rahman also stressed the need to develop separate codes of conduct for editors and owners, alongside those for journalists. He expressed the expectation that advocacy for news media self-regulation would continue under MRDI’s five-year Strategic Action Plan on Advocacy for News Media Reform in Bangladesh (2025–2030).
The consultation included policy discussions on the status of implementation of the Media Reform Commission’s recommendations and the way forward.
Participants said the recommendations, developed through consultations with journalists, editors, owners and civil society representatives across the country, required transparent, coordinated and time-bound implementation.
They said reform efforts should not be limited to selected issues but should pursue fundamental structural change. Comprehensive reform of laws, policies and institutional frameworks could help protect editorial independence, ensure financial security and restore public trust.
Participants also highlighted the need for regular reviews of reform progress and continued dialogue among stakeholders.
Kamal Ahmed, former chief of the Media Reform Commission and consulting editor at The Daily Star, said the recommendations reflected a consensus across the media industry, including editors, owners and working journalists.
“The recommendations of the Media Reform Commission reflect the consensus of the entire industry, including editors, owners and working journalists. Piecemeal amendments to laws will not resolve the ongoing anarchy in the media landscape; what is required is comprehensive structural reform. We must establish an independent permanent media commission and build self-regulation on the foundation of our own ethical code of conduct,” he said.
“If we fail to regulate ourselves, the government will inevitably step in with restrictive and coercive legal controls by using laws like the recent draft cyber act,” he added.
Participants agreed that sustainable self-regulation required strong and independent editorial policies capable of resisting pressure from the government, media owners, advertisers and political actors.
Rejoanul Haq Raja, director of news and current affairs at Channel S, said professional and credible journalism was essential to resisting external pressure.
“The more authentic and professional our journalism is, the greater courage and strength we will have to withstand external pressure. This is the essence of self-regulation. Before demanding accountability from others, we must first establish our own internal accountability. Only when we hold ourselves accountable can we speak with authority about others,” he said.
On journalists’ working conditions, participants said ethical journalism could not be separated from financial security. They called on media owners to ensure timely salary payments, formal appointment letters, lawful benefits and safe working environments.
Participants also stressed the need to give greater consideration to the experiences and realities of community news outlets and journalists outside Dhaka in national-level discussions and policy initiatives on media self-regulation.
They emphasized the importance of developing an effective, practical and inclusive self-regulation framework that accounts for the diverse realities of news media across Bangladesh.

item.title: Winter vegetables arrive in Rajshahi, but prices remain high
item.description:
Early winter vegetables have started arriving in Rajshahi’s wholesale and retail markets, but high prices continue to put pressure on consumers.
A visit to Saheb Bazar Mashtarpatti kitchen market on Sunday morning found a growing variety of winter vegetables, though many remained beyond the reach of ordinary buyers.
Pui shak was selling for Tk10 per kg, while red amaranth and potatoes cost Tk20, papaya Tk25, pointed gourd, taro and elephant foot yam Tk40, onions Tk45, and radish and spiny gourd Tk50 per kg.
Okra and taro stems were selling for Tk60 per kg, while yardlong beans, bitter gourd and cucumber cost Tk70. White eggplant and cauliflower were priced at Tk80 per kg.
Red eggplant and garlic were selling for Tk100 per kg, while green chillies and carrots cost Tk120, beans Tk140, and ginger and tomatoes Tk160. Green bananas were priced at Tk30 for four, while each bottle gourd cost Tk30.
Consumer Anwar Hossain said prices had yet to fall despite the arrival of winter vegetables. Although some items were relatively cheap, the high prices of others made it difficult for consumers to buy a variety of vegetables at once.
Vegetable trader Alauddin said supplies had not increased enough to bring prices down. He expected prices to fall as more produce reached the markets.
Meanwhile, farmers in Paba upazila are expanding early-season vegetable cultivation to take advantage of higher prices before regular winter supplies arrive.
Mosharraf Hossain, a farmer in Paba, said early-season cultivation involved risks, including the potential loss of around 2,000 cauliflower or cabbage plants per bigha. However, farmers could earn substantial profits if they brought their produce to market on time.
He said he had sold cauliflower grown on three bighas and cabbage grown on four-and-a-half bighas at Tk60-70 per head, with prices sometimes reaching Tk90. After deducting production costs, he earned around Tk150,000 per bigha. He is now cultivating cabbage on another 25 bighas.
Another farmer, Nazrul Islam of Alimganj, has grown 4,000 early-season cabbage plants on 12 kathas of land at a cost of Tk18,000-20,000. He has already sold 200 heads at Tk30 each and expects to earn around Tk100,000 from the remaining crop, with a projected profit of Tk80,000 after expenses.
Nazrul said he had earned around Tk500,000 by growing tomatoes on five bighas last year. This season, following advice from the agriculture department, he has planted early-season tomatoes on 10 kathas.
Early-season cauliflower, cabbage, beans, radishes, carrots, eggplants, bottle gourds and leafy vegetables are being cultivated in several areas of Paba, including Haripur, Harian, Damkura, Parila, Borgaichi, Naohata and Paikpara.
Paba Upazila Agriculture Officer MA Mannan said the upazila had already met its seasonal target of cultivating vegetables on 1,895 hectares, with early-season varieties accounting for a significant share.
He said farmers were being encouraged to grow early-season vegetables and advised to use biological pesticides, applying chemical pesticides only at approved doses.
Mustafa Kamal Hossain, deputy director of the Department of Agricultural Extension in Rajshahi, said the district had set a target of cultivating vegetables on 6,430 hectares this season. Early-season vegetable cultivation had increased by 200 hectares compared with previous years, he added.

item.title: Ex-MP Abdul Mannan sent to jail in anti-terrorism case
item.description:
A Dhaka court on Sunday ordered former Meherpur-1 MP Professor Abdul Mannan to be sent to jail after rejecting his bail petition in an anti-terrorism case.
Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Ariful Islam passed the order, said SI Arif Reza of the prosecution department.
Earlier on Sunday, Detective Branch (DB) police arrested Abdul Mannan from his residence in Dhanmondi at around 6am.
Investigation officer Inspector Md Masudur Rahman of the Tejgaon Zonal Team produced him before the court and sought an order to keep him in jail. Lawyer Al Imran Mukul, representing Abdul Mannan, sought bail, while the prosecution opposed the application.
After the hearing, the court rejected the bail petition and ordered him to be sent to jail. However, Abdul Mannan was not produced in the courtroom during the hearing.
According to the case statement, on the morning of June 18, 35-40 leaders and activists of the banned Awami League and Bangladesh Chhatra League, including Nibas Majumder, brought out a procession near Mohakhali Bus Terminal under the jurisdiction of Tejgaon Industrial Area police station.
The allegations state that the procession involved anti-government slogans and crude bomb explosions, causing panic among the public and involving anti-state activities.
On the same day, Sub-Inspector Mohammad Zahidul Haque of Tejgaon Industrial Area police station filed the case.

item.title: President stresses improved textile education to reduce reliance on foreign experts
item.description:
President Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir on Sunday stressed the need to improve textile education and research to produce internationally competitive engineers and specialists and reduce the sector’s dependence on foreign experts.
He made the remarks when a seven-member delegation led by Bangladesh University of Textiles (BUTEX) Vice-Chancellor Prof Dr Md Julhas Uddin paid a courtesy call on him at Bangabhaban.
Describing textiles as one of the country’s major economic sectors, the president emphasised ensuring suitable employment opportunities at home and abroad for textile graduates.
This would help make proper use of the country’s skilled human resources while earning foreign currency, he said, underscoring the need to increase domestic cotton production to meet the raw material requirements of the textile industry.
He called for taking steps to encourage farmers, explore ways to reduce production costs and strengthen coordination between the agriculture and textile sectors.
He further stressed the need for more research into extracting fibres from natural sources, including jute, pineapple leaves and banana plants, alongside the development of synthetic yarn.
During the meeting, the delegation briefed the president on BUTEX’s contributions to the development of the country’s textile and readymade garment industries, as well as its academic and research activities.
They also highlighted several issues requiring attention, including infrastructure development, the establishment of modern laboratories, recruitment of additional staff, the creation of a separate BCS (Textile) cadre, increased budgetary allocations and the allocation of land in Purbachal, Dhaka, for a second campus.
The president listened to their concerns and advised them to contact the relevant ministries to resolve the issues. He also assured the delegation of his cooperation.
During the meeting, the VC invited the president, also the chancellor of the university, to preside over BUTEX’s second convocation, scheduled for March next year.
The president accepted the invitation and assured the delegation that he would attend the event.
